Okay, here’s what I found and what we need to do.

You’ve got a GPU that’s too small for both dictation and a big TTS model at the same time. Right now, when you use the TTS, it crashes the dictation because it’s using too much memory. The old GPU—your GTX 1060—isn’t big enough for any useful local LLM or TTS model, so we’re stuck reloading everything every time.

The best way to fix this is to use a cloud model for quick summaries. It’ll only take about a second to start speaking, and it won’t interfere with your dictation. The text would go to a separate cloud API, like Haiku 5.5, and then it’d speak the summary straight away.

For the voice, we’d use a small local model called Kokoro on the old GPU. It’s good quality and doesn’t use the main PC’s GPU, so it won’t slow down your dictation. If you don’t want to use cloud models, we could keep everything local—but then you’d have to deal with the GPU not being big enough for both things at once.

Should I set up the cloud model and Kokoro, or would you prefer to keep everything local?
